summary: Bitcoin has been in freefall since June 2, sliding to $61,655 by June 4 — its lowest level in months — wiping out roughly $1.8 billion in leveraged positions. The crash was triggered by a confluence of events: Strategy disclosed its first net Bitcoin sale since December 2022, and while the 32 BTC sold was negligible in size, the symbolic breach of its "never sell" narrative shook investor confidence.
tweet: Strategy's first BTC sale in years sparked $1.8B in crypto liquidations as Iran tensions and sticky inflation push yields higher — crypto craters while stocks hold on AI momentum.
